name: Ratify the interim two-partner decision rule
text_content:
Type: founder decision

Source: Session 3 of the Scaling People translation program, page section 4.4 of the S3 page in the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253. Session task 86ajgmhgx.

Until the chef seat is filled there are two partners and two equal votes have no majority. The team's argued interim: for every decision outside the reserved classes, the domain owner decides after consulting the other partner where the consequence crosses domains; for reserved-class decisions, both partners or neither, with the status quo as the default when they disagree, so a disagreement is a hold rather than a deadlock; and the lunch decision is frozen, not held, because the record makes it three-partner and two cannot take it. Requires Dominic. The operating agreement must be read first for any voting rule it already holds. Extends the existing founder decision on the three-partner deadlock rule.

comment.text:
Extended by Session 15. The decision about a person's staying, which Session 14 recommended adding to the reserved classes, is now designed in full as a class: inputs only the hand-off package or the non-negotiable line with the flag's record and the person's words; both partners and counsel present; the mode line on the center's mechanisms first; both or neither with the status quo as staying; stays, stays with a move offered, or leaves on a date; the next review's agenda with a hold of at most one review; a closed record in no one's voice (S15 P22, 10.4). A departure of the third kind, a seat retired with its holder in it and no open move chosen, is decided as the Class A structure change it already is, with counsel (S15 P24). Row 189 fails until both are ratified.

Filed by Session 15 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmjpw. Reasoning lives on the S15 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

The rule is beneath every partners' review entry on the S14 page and the entries are marked incomplete until it is ratified. S14 page, sections 12.3 and 12.7; P26, P39.
